If you are comparing nyama choma grills for sale, ours is built heavier than a typical jua kali grill so it survives years of weekend rushes.

sections.heading: Key Features and Benefits
sections.body:
Deep rectangular firebox. It holds a good bed of charcoal, so heat stays steady through a long evening and you are not constantly topping up.

Strong grate bars. They carry goat, beef, chicken and sausages and leave the grill marks customers expect, so your meat looks as good as it tastes.

Raised side bars. Rest meat higher above the coals to finish slowly or keep it warm while you serve, so nothing gets overcooked during a rush.

sections.heading: Who It Suits and Where It Is Used
sections.body:
It suits butcheries that roast meat for customers, bars and nyama choma joints, restaurants with an outdoor grill area, caterers at weddings and functions, and homes that host family gatherings.

Because it is simple and tough, it also works well for roadside choma stalls and weekend events where the grill is moved and set up often.

sections.heading: How to Roast Great Nyama Choma
sections.body: Light the charcoal and wait until it is covered in white ash before you put meat on. Spread the coals so one side is hotter than the other. Sear the meat over the hot side, then move it to the cooler side or onto the raised bars to cook through slowly. Salt the meat lightly and avoid pressing it, so it stays juicy. Serve with kachumbari and ugali.

sections.heading: Charcoal Grill or Gas?
sections.body: Charcoal gives the smoky flavour that defines nyama choma, which is why most Kenyan grills still use it. It also needs no gas cylinder or electricity. Gas grills heat up faster but do not give the same taste.

sections.heading: What to Check Before Buying
sections.body: Decide where the grill will stand: it should be outdoors or under an open shelter with good airflow. Plan how much meat you roast at peak times so you choose the right size, and keep a dry store for charcoal.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Never use a charcoal grill inside a closed room, because burning charcoal produces carbon monoxide. Keep the grill away from walls, roofs and anything that can catch fire, and keep children at a safe distance. Use long tongs and heat-proof gloves.

sections.heading: Care and Maintenance
sections.body: Brush the grate while it is still warm to remove fat and burnt bits. Empty cold ash regularly so air can reach the coals. Keep the grill covered or under shelter when not in use and repaint any rusty spots.

sections.body: A lidded charcoal grill opens up a wider menu than an open grill.
